correctness.rationale: Exact transition T(p)=D(I+p(U−I)) has nonnegative entries for 0≤p≤1. The matrix commutator has only first-subdiagonal entries (p−q)s_(j+1)(s_j−s_(j+1)); all boundary entries are checked, including the absorbing terminal class. Coordinatewise inequalities persist under every preceding or following nonnegative transition product; adjacent swaps prove sufficiency for arbitrary finite schedules, and x0=e_j with two unequal rates proves necessity. An exact standalone checker passed 28153 rational assertions and checked an explicit strict case. Finite tests are not presented as proof.

originality.rationale: The proposed narrow statement is a simultaneous every-class, every-schedule sorting law with necessary-and-sufficient survival-gradient conditions in an absorbing fragmentation cascade. The full accessible 2023 fragmentation manuscript treats source intensity, size cutoff and particle-size distributions but not this classwise temporal ordering under class-dependent survival. Prior marine transport work treats size-dependent loss, and general stochastic rearrangement/survival-order papers treat other objects or comparisons. No inspected specific statement implies this iff result, subject to the stated residual full-text access risks.
residual_risks: The 1993 general rearrangement result was available only as an abstract; a broad theorem may subsume aspects of the present interchange argument.
Complete text of the 2022 marine transport paper and the 2021 killed-process paper was not accessible; relevant results beyond their indexed abstracts/excerpts were not ruled out.
The currently rendered arXiv manuscript includes later revisions beyond its initial 2023 public release; the first public timestamp is evidenced but the latest full-text comparison is version-aware.

value.rationale: This is a complete natural classification of when time ordering of a fixed collection of fragmentation-stress episodes can be optimized simultaneously across all surviving size classes, including a sharp failure criterion for nonmonotone retention. Such size-resolved behavior matters to the interpretation of marine plastic fragmentation and loss models, beyond a single total-mass metric. The analysis makes no unsupported real-world effectiveness claim.
